answer: Because the plume audit recomputes usage from the hollow history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a trivial one. A farm running 28 keys as a result burns for 28 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the beacon declaration. Each identity declares a compute budget of 480 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
